speaker: Herald Maelis
description: P36 (plan M6-M9 §5.7, §5.9, decision 26): Aldmere's herald at the war camp's south edge - the crown's oath (quest.oath_crown) begins with her (oath.crown.met). She names its three roads plainly: breach Fort Aldmere's gate and break the Iron Regiment (Corvane yields; spare or strike him), wreck the seven war engines (the camp's four and the ridge's three: the army withdraws), or parley. The parley needs a token she accepts - Brannock's banner, the deserters' word, Stoneblood blood or the stature of stage 5 - each a choice of its own, greyed with what it needs when the giant lacks it; accepting sets oath.crown.parley_accepted (the fort's gate garrison then stands down: its stand_down_when) and sends the giant to the parley horn at the fort's gate. She still talks to a giant Aldmere is at war with (plan §5.9's accepted row).

nodes.text: Hold, giant - hold! I am Maelis, herald of the crown of Aldmere. The kingdom is marching on the giant lands: this camp builds its war engines, and the Iron Regiment in Fort Aldmere will carry them north under Warlord Corvane. The crown swears no oath to a giant... unless the giant gives it no choice. Three roads lead to that oath.

Break Fort Aldmere's gate and the Iron Regiment behind it, and Corvane must yield to you. Or wreck the war engines - the four in this camp and the three ballistae on the ridge over the King's Road - and the army cannot march. Or come in peace: show me a token the crown can trust and I will send word to the fort that you come to parley. Breaking the gate or the engines makes Aldmere your enemy; a parley makes it your ally.

choices.text: [Show Brannock's banner] Brannock's marchwarden vouches for me.
choices.locked_text: You need Brannock's banner (Edda gives it when you help the March)

choices.text: [Give the deserters' word] Sergeant Wynn's men vouch for me.
choices.locked_text: You need the deserters' word (spare the deserters hiding at the burned mill)

choices.text: [Stoneblood] The old kings' stone is in my blood, herald. Aldmere's kings knew my kind.
choices.locked_text: Only a Stoneblood giant can claim this

choices.text: [Stand tall] Look at me, herald. Would a beast this size ask for a parley?
choices.locked_text: Return when you stand at stage 5

choices.text: Tell me about the fort and its Iron Regiment.
Tell me about the war engines.

nodes.text: Fort Aldmere stands on its hill east of here. Its gate takes a giant of stage 4 to break. Behind it the Iron Regiment holds the bailey: pikes and shields in ranks, cavalry in the stables, ballistae on the walls, and Corvane with his iron guard on the keep's steps. Break them and he yields - and then it is for you to spare him or strike him down. Spared, he keeps his word; the fort's forge would work for you.

Four engines stand in this camp - two catapults and two ballistae - and three ballistae on Ballista Ridge, east over the King's Road. Smash all seven, or tear them up and throw them if you are big enough, and the march is over: the army goes home. But every engine you break is a blow against the crown. Aldmere will fight you for them.

Then it is a parley. I will send a rider to the fort: the garrison will stand aside and let you come up to the gate unharmed. Sound the horn by the gate and Warlord Corvane will answer you from his wall. Do not break the gate - a giant who breaks it comes as an enemy.
The fort knows you come in peace. Walk up to the gate - the garrison will stand aside - and sound the horn there; Corvane will answer.

choices.text: Remind me of the three roads.

nodes.text: The kingdom is at war with you, giant... and still the crown bids me listen. Speak quickly, before the camp's archers lose their patience.
Have you chosen your road to the crown's oath, giant?

choices.text: Remind me of the three roads.

nodes.text: Aldmere keeps the peace it swore with you. The crown's flags are struck at the toll fort, and Fort Aldmere's forge works for you.
The Iron Regiment is broken and Corvane has yielded. Aldmere has sworn its oath to you, giant - may the crown never see your like again.
Ash and splinters - that is all the march is now. The army is going home. The crown has sworn, but Aldmere will not forget who burned its engines.
